candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is fibroadenoma, which in this ectopic anal location would represent a benign biphasic tumor with both epithelial and stromal components, analogous to breast fibroadenoma arising from ectopic breast tissue. Leiomyoma is a smooth muscle neoplasm and is a separate diagnostic entity. Although leiomyoma can occur in the anal canal and shares some gross features (firm, well-circumscribed, gray-white), it does not fulfill the histological definition of fibroadenoma. The clinical details (20-year slow growth, firm fibrotic consistency, encapsulated, gray-white cut surface, distal anal canal location) are consistent with fibroadenoma of ectopic breast tissue, not leiomyoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Leiomyoma is a smooth muscle tumor; fibroadenoma is a biphasic epithelial-stromal tumor (classically of breast-type tissue); both are benign but represent distinct histological entities

case_quality_flags: Fibroadenoma at the anal canal is a rare entity likely arising from ectopic breast tissue (accessory mammary tissue along the milk line); the reference diagnosis is unusual but clinically plausible given the location and morphology
Leiomyoma is a common differential for firm anal canal polyps and shares gross features, making histopathological confirmation critical for definitive diagnosis
